h1: Angle rolls, tube rollers and section benders
intro: An angle roll (also called a roll bender, section bender, profile bender, ring roller or tube roller) pushes a bar, angle, pipe, tube or beam between three rolls to bend it into an arc, a ring or a spiral — the machine behind curved handrails, tank stiffener rings, rolled flanges, arched trusses and coiled heating pipe. Şahinler builds the complete range: the motorized PK 30 and PK 35 for small flat bar, angle and tube, the hydraulic HPK 40 to HPK 120 section and pipe benders with digital readouts, hydraulic guides and optional NC control, the HPK DP heavy-duty beam benders for channel, I-beam and H-beam up to HEB 600, and the TC-42 NC coiling machine for variable-pitch tube coils. Every machine rolls horizontally or vertically, comes with a standard roll set and takes pipe, tube, angle and special profile rolls; capacity charts for each model are on this page. Sold with a CSA-approved panel, parts and support from Mississauga, ON.

faq.q: Angle roll, roll bender, section bender, ring roller, tube roller — are these the same machine?
faq.a: Yes. All describe the three-roll machine on this page: two driven rolls hold the section and the third roll pushes it into a curve, and a ring is finished by running the piece round again. Each profile — flat bar, angle, square bar, pipe, tube, channel, beam — has its own roll set; the capacity chart under each model lists the largest section it rolls and the smallest diameter it rolls it to.

faq.q: How do I read the capacity chart?
faq.a: Find your profile in the left column and read the largest section the machine can roll and, after the arrow, the minimum outside diameter it can roll that section to. A second entry gives a smaller section with its tighter minimum diameter. 'Standard rolls' profiles are rolled with the roll set supplied with the machine; 'optional rolls' need the matching roll set. The chart is for mild steel of 37,700 psi yield; stainless, aluminum and high-strength sections need the next model up.

faq.q: Which angle roll do I need for 2″ pipe or 2 × 2 × 1/4″ angle?
faq.a: The HPK 50 rolls NPS 2 pipe to a Ø39″ ring and L 2 × 2 × 1/4″ angle leg-out to Ø24″; the HPK 60 does the same with more margin and takes NPS 3 pipe and L 2-3/4 × 2-3/4 × 1/4″. For a smaller ring in the same section, or for daily production, step up one size — the minimum diameter shrinks and the rolls last longer.

faq.q: Horizontal or vertical — what is the difference?
faq.a: The HPK 40 to HPK 120 and the PK 35 work in both positions. Vertical takes less floor space and suits short pieces and rings; horizontal lets long bars, pipe and beams run out over the floor on supports and is the only position on the HPK DP machines. Lateral guide rolls (manual or hydraulic) keep the section square to the rolls and stop twist on angle and channel.

faq.q: Can these machines roll spirals and coils?
faq.a: Yes. Every HPK with the optional spiral bending crane rolls spiral staircases, stringers and heating coils; the TC-42 NC is the dedicated coiling machine that rolls variable-pitch coils with a straight elbow at each end in one automatic pass.

faq.q: Do you supply the rolls for my profile?
faq.a: A standard roll set comes with every machine and rolls flat bar, square bar and tee. Pipe, tube, angle, channel and special profile rolls are quoted to your section drawing and shipped with the machine or added later; Delrin rolls are available for polished stainless and aluminum.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.
